title: Iki environment (iki/v1)
description: What a plugin's actions need to run, wherever they run: software, the smallest machine, and data volumes. Each deployment binds it to its own compute templates.

tiers.description: The compute tiers it can run on.

resources.description: The smallest machine its actions run on.

image.description: The container image with its registry, pinned by its digest (`ghcr.io/acme/alphafold@sha256:…`). The container and vm tiers run it, and so does the client tier when people have Docker or Podman.

python.description: A Python virtual environment, for the backend and client tiers.

requirements.description: A requirements file in the plugin, every package pinned with `==` and its `--hash`, as `uv pip compile --generate-hashes` writes it.

conda.description: A conda environment, for the backend and client tiers.

lockfile.description: An explicit lockfile in the plugin, every package with its hash, as `conda-lock` or `conda list --explicit --md5` writes it.

volumes.description: Data volumes its actions read, such as reference databases, by name.

setup.description: A script that fills its volumes once, when the environment is built. Its runs are recorded as data versions.

requires_approval.description: A compute admin approves each build before it starts, for setups that cost a lot.

network.description: The hosts the setup may download from.

name.description: A name in kebab-case, such as `alphafold-gpu`.

file.description: A path in the plugin, relative to its root.

quantity.description: An amount of memory or disk, such as `512Mi`, `64Gi` or `3Ti`.

min_memory.description: The memory each GPU must have.

scratch_disk.description: Local disk for the run's working files.

access.description: `read_only_many` (the default): many runs read it at once. `read_write_once`: one run at a time may change it.

performance.description: What the data needs from the disk: `standard` (the default), `high_iops` for many small reads, or `high_throughput` for large ones.

mount.description: Where runs see it: an absolute path.
